# dsh-leafy-skin

An eye-friendly green skin: a leafy palette layered over the official DSH web GUI theme, in a
light
emerald and a dark mint variant.
> I wanted the effect of a Minecraft resource pack.
**English** | 中文
## Compatibility
| Plugin version | DSH version |

## Features

- **Layered greens** — a mist-green canvas, raised panels, and a deeper sidebar, with emerald
accent

s in light mode and mint in dark, instead of one flat wash of green.
- **Comfortable by construction

** — no pure white or pure black, a single green hue family, and
all body text at WCAG AA (≥ 4.5:1).

- **Texture** — softer corner radii, green-tinted diffuse shadows, low-contrast hairlines, and
glas

sy menu surfaces.
- **Details** — mint text selection, Inter / Noto Sans SC / Cascadia Code font sta

cks, slim
scrollbars, and restrained hover and menu motion.
- **Tunable** — the palette is one comme

nted table, a self-check script guards contrast, and the
style layer has a single on/off switch.

## Usage

Install the plugin and load the app. The skin layers itself over the active theme, so light, dark,
a
nd follow-system each pick up their own variant automatically.
## Customize

- **Colours** — the `TOKENS` table in `lib/client.js`, grouped and commented by area.
- **Radii, sha

dows, fonts, motion** — the same file, plus the small style layer below it.
- **Palette only** — set

`ENABLE_CSS_LAYER` to `false` in `lib/client.js` to drop the style layer
entirely.
- **Check your w

ork** — `node tools/check-palette.mjs` validates token shape, the boot colour
match, text and syntax

contrast (including translucent surfaces and the focus ring), and the
style layer's three constrain

ts.
- **Coverage matrix** — `node tools/audit-tokens.mjs` reads the installed DSH and lists every
`-

-dsw-*` token it declares: whether this skin covers it directly or through a `var()` chain,
and how

often official bundles consume it. `--strict` fails on tokens that are used but covered
by neither t

he palette nor a written reason.
- **Stable hooks** — `node tools/check-hooks.mjs` confirms the `dat

a-*` hooks the style layer
relies on still exist upstream, so a DSH upgrade breaks the check instead

## Uninstall
Any one of these, then restart DSH:

1. Comment out the `insert` entry in `cordis.patch.yml`;
2. Drop `dsh-leafy-skin` from `dsh.profile.

bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`;
3. Run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-le

n `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`;
3. Run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-leafy-skin`.
## Known limitations

- The native window title bar belongs to the DSH desktop shell, not to this plugin, so it stays
DSH

grey for the instant before the page paints.
- Real see-through glass is impossible on Windows — the

sidebar depth and translucent menus are
colour layering, not blur through the window.
- Components

hard-code font sizes and layout in hashed CSS modules, so this skin deliberately
leaves them alone.
